If Nintendo manage to build more third-party support the console would have a wider appeal, however I prefer to experience cross-platform titles on the PC and buy Nintendo consoles for Nintendo games. As an owner of a Wii U, I would like to see Nintendo retain the same level of high quality first party releases as they have this generation.

If they can manage that (and have a stronger launch line-up than the Wii U) it will more than likely have a place in my living room not long after release.

I have owned practically every one of Nintendo's consoles and hand-helds at one time or another. The main thing that always makes me come back to Nintendo is the quality of their first party titles. I don't care about 3rd party titles showing up on the NX. I don't care about high performance hardware, most Nintendo IPs take place in cartoony worlds so realism doesn't really matter.

I also have always liked the quality and longevity of their hardware. I still have my original Game Boy that I got 22 years ago and it works just fine. I know that whatever I get will last forever with some care. I've only seen 2 Nintendo product break, a Game Cube controller that I spiked on the ground, and a friend's DS that he slammed on his little brother's head.

All I want is a no gimmicks, performance-oriented Nintendo console that can also get support for more third party games. Add full backwards compatibility for Wii, WiiU and maybe even gamecube games. Nintendo should also consider virtual reality, similar to the occulus rift for the new console. The most important thing is for Nintendo to have a good lineup of launch titles ready to get people excited.
